newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK November PMI survey.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK November PMI survey.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to the UK November PMI survey published at 0930 GMT.
The index fell to 54.4 percent from 54.5 pct in October.
"It's slightly disappointing. It does show the manufacturing sector is recovering but the recovery doesn't seem to be gathering momentum."

"The most significant aspect is the price component, which clearly shows even though the manfacturing sector is recovering, inflation pressures still remain very subdued and that should be very encouraging. I think it'll be very encouraging for the Chancellor. These figures...will take any immediate pressure off the Chancellor to raise interest rates."

"There are some potential upside risks in the UK economy. There are differences between the recovery in the U.S. and UK. The UK recovery is built around recovery in the consumer sector and the signs are consumer growth will be well above that in the U.S. There is a risk the Chancellor will miss the RPIX target, but if he does it will not be by a great deal...and he may be prepared to tough it out at next week's meeting (and leave rates on hold)."

"It's a little bit disappointing. I think there is a sterling story coming through there. From a policy perspective, it's reasonably favourable news for the Chancellor but I don't think it changes the underlying picture that the manufacturing recovery will be in full swing by next year.
It's pretty good news from a gilts perspective, but may be temporary."

"Though the PMI price index fell, this was due to likely temporary sterling strength. (The survey is) sterling positive and gilt and short sterling negative, though we do not think the market rate forecasts will be realised. The Chancellor hopes tight fiscal policy will avoid sharp monetary tightening. And his insistance that his 2.5 percent inflation target will be met, though not credible, suggests little reason for the hikes priced in."
